title: Weather at Gale (REMS)

values.label: Air temperature (diurnal range, 1.6 m boom)
values.note: Typical diurnal cycle (~190 K nighttime low to ~270 K daytime high, Gómez-Elvira et al. 2014).

values.label: Ground brightness temperature (diurnal range)
values.note: Typical diurnal cycle (~183 K pre-dawn to ~290 K midday, Gómez-Elvira et al. 2014).

limits.label: Water triple-point context
limits.source: Gale surface pressure (700–920 Pa) straddles water's triple point; unsuited human survival impossible

limits.label: Walk-scale spatial weather map
limits.source: REMS is a single rover-local weather station; Mars Climate Database v6.2 is 5.625° × 3.75° (~330 × 220 km)

note: REMS is a rover-local meteorological station on Curiosity; no walk-scale spatial weather map or live forecast exists for Gale Crater. Values represent observed Gale climatology.
claim_boundary: Context card only — never interpolated into per-cell route weather maps. Excursion thermal/dust windows derived from climatology are Scenario assumptions.
source: Gómez-Elvira et al. 2012, Space Sci Rev, doi:10.1007/s11214-012-9921-1; Gómez-Elvira et al. 2014, JGR-Planets, doi:10.1002/2013JE004576; Haberle et al. 2014, JGR-Planets, doi:10.1002/2013JE004488; PDS4 urn:nasa:pds:msl_rems_bundle
date_range: 2012-08-07 → 2026 (PDS4 urn:nasa:pds:msl_rems_bundle sols 1–4843; Gómez-Elvira et al. 2014 baseline)
